comparison: Both strongly support that epidermal cell stimulation activates nociceptive sensory neurons and evokes behavioral responses. OpenEval emphasizes optogenetic/thermogenetic evidence with multiple GAL4 drivers (C3, C4, C23, C24, C28, C29, C31, C32, C33), while peer review focuses on the main claim validation (C3, C4, C23, C24, C28) and includes behavioral diversity claims (C38, C39, C45, C49). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED with high confidence.

OpenEval R2 addresses behavioral diversity and temporal dynamics (C38-C49) showing broader/prolonged epidermis-evoked responses. Peer R1 partially overlaps (C38, C39, C45, C49) as part of overall evidence for epidermal activation of sensory neurons. Both are SUPPORTED, though OpenEval provides more detailed analysis of behavioral quantification.

Both address calcium imaging evidence for epidermis-neuron coupling. OpenEval R3 focuses on neuronal activation and tetanus toxin experiments (C50-C54, C58), while peer R2 accepts calcium imaging findings (C50-C52, C58, C130) as complementary to behavioral studies. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED without challenge.

Both address tetanus toxin experiments demonstrating requirement for neuronal output. OpenEval R3 includes broader calcium imaging context (C50-C54, C58), while peer R3 specifically validates tetanus toxin results (C53, C54, C131). Both are SUPPORTED as part of epidermis-neuron coupling evidence.

Perfect alignment on synergistic effects of combined epidermis-nociceptor stimulation (C59-C66). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED, with OpenEval emphasizing quantitative measurements and statistical significance, while peer review accepts findings as convincing evidence for epidermal cell role in nociceptive activation.

Both strongly support sensitization findings. OpenEval R5 focuses on time course quantification and specificity (C67-C71), while peer R5 includes broader context (C7, C8, C67-C71, C110) and treats this as a key advance in mechanosensation understanding. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED.

Strong agreement on intrinsic mechanosensitivity of epidermal cells. Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval R6 emphasizes dose-dependent responses and multiple stimulus modalities (C5, C74-C81), while peer R6 confirms the main claim with similar claim coverage (C5, C74-C76, C80, C81).

Both strongly support Stim/Orai mechanism with convergent evidence. OpenEval R7 details genetic, pharmacological, and imaging approaches (C6, C83, C87-C96), while peer R7 emphasizes novelty and significance (C6, C83, C89-C91, C95, C116, C119, C154). Both are SUPPORTED and treat this as a major discovery.

Partial overlap on SOCE mechanism. OpenEval R7 includes pharmacological and zero-calcium experiments (C87, C88, C92-C94) as part of comprehensive Stim/Orai evidence. Peer R8 rates these claims as UNCERTAIN, noting unresolved questions about how mechanical stimulation triggers ER calcium release, despite accepting that both components contribute.

Perfect alignment on human keratinocyte data (C97-C99). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes translational relevance with species-specific differences in mechanosensitivity thresholds, while peer review highlights conservation across species as supporting broader significance.

Perfect alignment on gain-of-function experiments (C100, C101). Both evaluations are SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes these complement loss-of-function data and are consistent with Orai channel properties, while peer review accepts them as part of thorough genetic analyses with appropriate controls.

Both address vesicular release in sensitization. OpenEval R10 is SUPPORTED with note about unidentified mediators (C103-C105, C132), while peer R11 is UNCERTAIN, raising concerns about reconciling SOCE kinetics with vesicular release requirements. Agreement on experimental observation but divergence on mechanistic interpretation.

Minimal overlap. OpenEval R10 addresses shibirets experiments (C103-C105, C132), while peer R12 accepts the overall epidermis-as-primary-sensor model (C105, C72, C9, C10, C108, C109). Both are SUPPORTED but address different aspects of the work.

Both address RNA-seq data from epidermal cells. OpenEval R11 focuses on absence of neurotransmitter biosynthesis genes but presence of vesicular machinery (C106, C107), while peer R14 accepts this molecular characterization (C82, C106, C107) as thorough genetic analysis. Both are SUPPORTED.

Both address RNA-seq expression data. OpenEval R12 focuses on ion channel expression (C82) as foundation for screening, while peer R14 accepts broader RNA-seq characterization (C82, C106, C107). Both are SUPPORTED as descriptive molecular evidence.

Both address morphometric control experiments. OpenEval R14 emphasizes ruling out developmental effects on nociceptor structure (C25), while peer R13 accepts these controls (C25, C33) as addressing potential confounds. Both are SUPPORTED.

Both address high-level conclusions about epidermal cells as primary mechanosensors. OpenEval R16 synthesizes multiple experimental findings (C9, C10, C72, C108-C110, C119), while peer R12 accepts the overall model (C72, C9, C10, C108, C109) as significant advance. Both are SUPPORTED.

Minimal overlap on sensitization conclusions. OpenEval R16 includes C110 as part of broader synthesis about selective effects on sensitization, while peer R5 includes C110 in context of prolonged escape rolling. Both are SUPPORTED.

Both address novelty and significance of Stim/Orai findings. OpenEval R17 focuses on summary statements about novelty (C116, C120, C154), while peer R7 emphasizes these same points (C116, C119, C154) as major discovery. Both are SUPPORTED with high confidence.

OpenEval R13 addresses Task6 RNAi screen results (C86) showing increased response to initial stimulus. No corresponding peer review evaluation found. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on behavioral screen data.

OpenEval R15 rates incomplete TnT blocking phenotypes (C55-C57) as UNCERTAIN, noting speculative interpretation about nervous system prioritization versus technical limitations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval R18 rates conservation claims (C123) as UNCERTAIN, noting that while SOCE is demonstrated in both species, functional conservation of the complete mechanism requires more extensive validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval R19 supports inference about nociceptor activation threshold (C36) based on prior work and current data, though direct quantification not provided. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval R20 supports hypothesis about differential SSN activation (C41) based on behavioral and calcium imaging data, noting mechanisms remain unclear. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval R21 supports inference about dose-dependent encoding (C136) but notes this remains hypothesis requiring direct testing of stimulus intensity relationships. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval R22 supports claims about ensheathment not being essential (C141, C142) based on C1da/Cho activation, but suggests conclusion may be too strong as sheaths could still modulate signaling. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval R23 rates speculative hypotheses about ensheathment functions (C143, C144) as UNCERTAIN, noting these are future research directions without experimental support. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval R24 supports extensive background claims from prior literature (C1, C2, C11-C22, C30, C34, C35, C37, C40, C73, C84, C85, C102, C111-C115, C117, C121, C122, C124-C129, C137, C139, C140, C145-C151) as accurate representations of cited work. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

OpenEval R25 supports explicit acknowledgments of limitations and future directions (C118, C133, C134, C152, C153), noting appropriate scientific rigor in distinguishing established findings from open questions. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.

Peer R2 accepts calcium imaging findings (C50-C52, C58, C130) as sophisticated complementary evidence. OpenEval R3 covers most of these claims but C130 appears only in peer review. Both are SUPPORTED.
Peer R3 accepts tetanus toxin experiments (C53, C54, C131) as part of epidermis-neuron coupling evidence. OpenEval R3 covers C53-C54 but C131 appears only in peer review. Both are SUPPORTED.
